narration: You got laid off. Savings? Ready. Resume? Polished. But there's one bill almost nobody budgets for — and it hits within two weeks.
visual: Person silhouette sitting at office desk, a termination letter floats down and lands. Dark background, amber accent lighting on the desk. Person looks up at the letter with shock.

narration: It's your COBRA health insurance bill. For a family of four, the average monthly premium is $1,778. Most people had zero idea coverage cost that much.
visual: Large white envelope opens to reveal a bill. The number $1,778 in bold red fills the screen. '/month' appears beneath it. Light background.

narration: At work, your employer quietly paid 70% of that premium. The second you leave, every dollar becomes yours — plus a two-percent admin fee on top.
visual: Pie chart splits: large sector labeled EMPLOYER (70%) in gray, small sector labeled YOU (30%) in red. Then the employer slice disappears, leaving only the YOU slice filling 100%. Dark background.

narration: Job searches take four to six months on average. At $1,778 a month, that's nearly eleven thousand dollars before you land your next paycheck.
visual: Six calendar pages line up across the screen, each flipping in sequence. Below them, a piggy bank visibly drains as a dollar counter climbs to $10,668. Light background.

narration: So 65% of laid-off workers just skip COBRA entirely. But one ER visit without insurance averages $2,200 for something minor — and $30,000 for anything serious.
visual: Hospital cross icon pulses. Two bill papers drop: one says $2,200, one says $30,000. A person silhouette sits in a waiting room chair, looking worried. Dark background.

narration: The fix: build your emergency fund to cover six months of COBRA, not just living expenses. Calculate your real number — it's probably twice what you think.
visual: Piggy bank with a red health cross on it fills up as a progress bar labeled 'COBRA FUND' grows from 0 to 6 months. Final text overlay: 'Your real emergency number.' Light background.
